title: Immunogenetic determinants of cancer risk
text:
With the revolutionary discovery of immunotherapy as a highly effective treatment for cancer, the immune
system, and specifically the interaction between CD8 T cells and HLA molecules, has emerged as an essential
player in cancer treatment, but its role in early tumorigenesis is understudied. Germline HLA heterozygosity
been shown to improve tumor immunogenicity and thus response to immunotherapy as well as lower
susceptibility to viral infection, but its role in cancer risk is unknown. This proposed research will use large,
diverse clinical and genomic datasets and an in vivo model of HLA-mediated immune surveillance to implicate
germline HLA zygosity in cancer risk, potentially identifying an important biomarker for increased cancer
screening, and provide insights into the mechanism of HLA-mediated immune surveillance of early tumors to
guide treatment and prevention strategies.

title: A High-Throughput Screening Platform to Discover RNA Methylation Inhibitors
text:
Adenosine methylation (m6A) is a highly prevalent RNA modification that has been linked to several human
cancers. The m6A methyltransferase complex has emerged as a potential therapeutic target; however, efforts to
identify methyltransferase inhibitors have been hampered by the lack of methods that provide a cellular readout
of adenosine methylation on a high-throughput scale. Here, we will develop a novel genetically encoded m6A
sensor system that provides a fluorescence-based readout for mRNA methylation which can be used both for
high-throughput drug discovery efforts as well as studies investigating m6A biology and its contribution to cancer.

title: Opioid-induced dysregulation of cortico-striatal circuits
text:
The incidence of reported heroin use and nonmedical prescription opioid use is on the rise in recent years,
with the rate of abuse in women increasing to a greater extent. The proposed studies will use a variety of
techniques to identify how opioids disrupt function of brain regions responsible for cognitive flexibility and
control over drug seeking behavior to identify substrates for the transition to opioid addiction and how factors
such as biological sex influence development of these functional adaptations.

title: Peptidome-Driven Algorithms for Faster and More Precise Mycobacterial Detection
text:
NTM infections are of growing concern due to the increasing number of NTM infections in the United States. The
need for precise identification of NTM at the species level has been prompted because the species level
detection could guide a more accurate treatment strategy. Our proposed algorithm-based peptidome method
can simultaneously identify NTM and predict macrolide susceptibility from clinical samples, greatly simplify NTM
diagnosis protocol with the subspecies identification resolution.

title: Genetic variant Evidence using Novel tools to Elucidate Pathophysiology: Accelerating Translation to Health (GenePath)
text: Understanding the precise impact of genetic variations that might have harmful effects in humans is essential for research and patient care. Our Coordinating Center will work with sites to create ML/AI variant characterization tools and organize and guide the creation of ELSI frameworks.

title: The lysosomal fasting response in intestinal stem cells and cancer
text:
Fasting interventions have numerous health benefits, but the underlying molecular mechanism remains less
explored. Here we focus on lysosomes, a dynamic signaling organelle that regulates cellular metabolism, protein
homeostasis, and metabolic adaptation – using the mammalian intestine as a paradigm, we will investigate how
lysosomes maintain intestinal stem cells and fuel tumorigenesis. Collectively, the goal of this proposal is to
leverage novel genetic and biochemical tools to uncover the downstream molecular effectors of lysosome
biology, which may have direct implications in developing stem cell regeneration and anti-tumor therapies to
improve human health.

title: Neuroimaging Training Program
text:
Investment in training of biomedical engineers to become experts in the development of non-
invasive imaging tools, for high and low resource communities, and their use in patients with
brain disorders such as depression, traumatic brain injury, and Alzheimer's Disease will advance
the ability to provide good medical care. The trainees from this program make significant
contributions to medical technologies that enable accurate diagnosis of illnesses and
determination of responses to treatments.

title: Development of the PAIN (Pain AI iNtervention) Platform for Patients at Home
text:
Opioid and analgesic overprescription, particularly in the surgical setting, can lead to opioid misuse and its
associated consequences. The individualization of pain medication regimens after surgery is an urgent matter
that can be approached by continuously monitoring the patient’s physiological response to pain using wearable
technology. This project aims to measure physiological variables (e.g., heart rate, respiratory rate) using a small
wearable device after surgery to create a pain biomarker that allows physicians to tailor pain medication to the
patient’s pain intensity, potentially decreasing the amount of prescribed medication and the risk of misuse.

title: Role of lipid metabolism in CD8+ T cell ferroptosis
text:
We will determine 1) how tumors and the tumor microenvironment accumulate fatty acids and use them
to induce lipid peroxidation in tumor-infiltrating CD8+ TTE or TEM cells; 2) how lipid peroxidation induces
CD8+ TTE or TEM cell ferroptosis and dysfunction in tumor beds, and 3) explore new methods to
counteract fatty acid effects and to restore T cell function in cancer patients. We hypothesize that
inhibiting T cell ferroptosis will effectively enhance the therapeutic efficacy of immunotherapy in cancer
patients. Completing this project will allow us and others to identify novel therapeutic targets and
develop new methods to improve the efficacy of current cancer immunotherapies.

title: A bioanalytical research program to unravel the human milk glycome
text:
Human milk oligosaccharides assist in promoting the healthy development of the brain, gut, and immune system
of infants and are produced in an infant-specific manner where biological responses drive their structures.
Unfortunately, existing analytical methodologies remain limited in fully separating all their isomeric permutations,
thus precluding their accurate structural characterization. To address these challenges, we will develop a
bioanalytical workflow consisting of a new multidimensional separations platform to be used in conjunction with
the development of chemical probes and gas-phase sequencing strategies.

title: Identifying pre-sepsis opportunities for early, targeted intervention
text:
Sepsis kills 11 million people every year and early identification and treatment are the only known ways to
improve mortality. We currently focus on treating people once they get to the hospital or emergency
department, which is often too late. This study will evaluate opportunities to identify and triage patients who
may be at high-risk of sepsis before they get to the hospital.

title: Unraveling effects of gut and blood microbial signatures on immune phenotypes and organ dysfunction in sepsis
text:
Sepsis is the leading cause of death in the intensive care units (ICU) and represents a dysregulated host
response to infection. The composition of the gut microbiota during sepsis and early in ICU course may
influence acute immune responses and ability to defend against subsequent infection. This investigation will
reveal how changes in the gut microbiota and their associated products that enter the blood influence immune
activation and exhaustion and organ dysfunction in acute and later stages of sepsis – findings that can inform
development of urgently needed new therapies.

title: Complementing broadly neutralizing antibodies and autologous responses to restrict virus escape and durably suppress HIV-1
text:
Project Narrative.
Virus resistance remains the central vulnerability of effective bnAb use in HIV. This application proposes to
address the problem of bNAb resistance by rationally selecting combination bNAb therapy that limits virus
escape. Our scientific premise is that in vivo mapping of virus escape from bNAbs, identification of
complementary bNAbs, defining the role of autologous antibodies, and rigorous in vivo testing in an authentic
NHP model will elucidate basic mechanisms of virus resistance to bNAbs and inform more effective use of
bNAbs across the HIV prevention, treatment and cure fields.

title: Core B:  Clinical Phenotyping and Technology Core
text: CORE B Lower respiratory tract infections cause 79% of deaths from infectious diseases in the United States. The international burden of pneumonia is even greater; pneumonia is the leading cause of death in resource- challenged countries and in the top 10 causes of death in the entire world. Viruses were increasingly recognized as a cause of community-acquired pneumonia (CAP), including in patients requiring mechanical ventilation or vasopressor therapy, even before the SARS-CoV-2 pandemic. The Core B will support testing the overall hypothesis of our PPG that the mortality and persistent organ failure in CAP, including influenza-, SARS-CoV-2, and other virus-induced CAP, represent a failure of resolution and lung repair. Mechanisms that underlie persistence of lung injury and progression of multiple organ dysfunction in the absence of pathogen persistence are incompletely understood, and all four projects in this proposal address this knowledge deficit with sophisticated animal models. The overarching goal of Core B is to validate findings from these murine models of influenza pneumonia in patients with severe CAP caused by viral pathogens and to provide support to all projects with statistical and bioinformatics analysis. Most CAP patients requiring mechanical ventilation (severe CAP) meet the definition of sepsis and the acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS). Recent data suggest that endotypes vary in sepsis and ARDS, with at least hypo- and hyper-inflammatory patterns, if not more. Unfortunately, most of these studies performed limited phenotyping of patients. In particular, discrimination between persistent infection versus persistent inflammation is not clear. For severe viral pneumonia, this includes not only viral clearance but assessment of the presence and clearance of bacterial superinfection. The major hypothesis of Core B is that human correlation of findings from murine influenza models requires careful and extensive clinical phenotyping. Core B will directly support the Specific Aims of each PPG Project with the following aims: Specific Aim 1. Provide bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) fluid from mechanically ventilated patients with severe viral pneumonia due to influenza A virus or SARS-CoV-2. Specific Aim 2. Define the microbiologic milieu at each BAL sampling time point. Specific Aim 3. Apply robust clinical phenotypes and relevant clinical endpoints. Specific Aim 4. Provide statistical and bioinformatics support. Ultimately, the goal of this PPG is to define immune system pathways and mechanisms of failed resolution and repair following viral pneumonia that are amenable to therapeutic interventions. Core B is integral to supporting this goal by demonstrating strong clinical correlations to findings from the proposed murine models.

title: First Aid Medicine to Treat Vesicant Induced Corneal Injury
text:
Chemical vesicant exposure poses a potential threat to our society. Currently, there are no effective
countermeasures to treat vesicant-induced corneal injury. This U01 aims to develop a novel protein therapeutic
that can be stockpiled and conveniently deployed to mitigate vesicant induced damages to the eye.

title: Developing a Novel Analytical Toolbox to Tackle Multifaceted Statistical Challenges in Analyzing Post-Fracture Recovery Trajectories in Older Adults with ADRD
text:
This project aims to develop an innovative analytical toolbox designed to address multifaceted statistical
challenges inherent in the analysis of real-world data. Utilizing this toolbox to analyze Medicare data will yield
insights into the identification of high-risk subgroups and hospital-level factors partially driving poor post-
fracture recovery trajectories for older adults living with ADRD. Consequently, these findings will enhance
predictive capabilities for multivariate and multilevel outcomes, enabling the development of personalized
caregiving strategies for new patients.

title: Designing biological light from scratch - a new paradigm for bioimaging and biosensing
text:
Bioluminescence technologies have emerged as a promising alternative to fluorescent proteins
for whole-animal imaging. However, the current availability of bioluminescent probes derived from
nature is inadequate for universal biomedical applications. Here, we combine de novo protein
design, synthetic chemistry, and deep learning to create a new form of biological light –
neoluminescence, which will enable multiplexed bioimaging and practical diagnostics.

title: T’Cher, Take Charge: A Increasing PrEP Awareness, Uptake, and Adherence Through Health Care Empowerment and Addressing Social Drivers of Health in the Deep South
text: Nearly half of high-risk populations in Louisiana are living with HIV and many face extreme social behavioral barriers creating risky environments and limiting access to life-saving HIV prevention. The proposed intervention is a combination of novel pilot components developed by experienced investigators to support PrEP awareness, uptake, and adherence in Louisiana. The proposed line of research has the potential to fill a large gap in PrEP interventions in U.S. Southern states where most new HIV cases occur and PrEP utilization is the lowest.

title: Next-Generation Native Ion Mobility-Mass Spectrometry Methods for the Characterization of Biotherapeutics
text:
Knowledge linking composition and structure in biopharmaceutical products is critical for our
understanding of their efficacy and safety. Understanding how such drugs interact with their
targets to create therapeutically-relevant complexes has been a central goal in biomedical
research and a host of structural biology and mass spectrometry methods have made great
progress in this endeavor, but we still lack sufficiently rapid and information rich technologies
capable of driving the discovery and development of next-generation biotherapeutics. Here, we
propose to develop a suite of new, rapid native ion mobility-mass spectrometry strategies capable
of simultaneously analyzing the sequences, modification status, higher order structures, and their
associated complexes using small amounts of unlabeled samples present within complex
mixtures that remain difficult or impossible to analyze using classical structural biology probes.

title: Investigating the role of endothelial cells in intestinal regeneration and disease
text:
Endothelial cells play a crucial role in supporting stem cell maintenance and regeneration in various tissues, yet
their contribution in intestinal repair and regeneration remains poorly understood. The goal of this proposal is to
investigate the function of blood endothelial cells and their secreted paracrine factors in intestinal repair, as well
as to determine changes in blood endothelial cells in inflammatory bowel disease. Findings from these studies
will have the potential to help develop strategies for modulating the endothelial cell niche to restore intestinal
function in the context of disease conditions.
